I have been working with wigs for quite a few years now. One thing I know is a good quality vs not so great quality wig. Let's take a look at this one.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?

HAIR
This wig has some great hair. the colors are definitely platinum white and what I would call light auburn base hairs. The white hairs are about 1/3 or so longer than the auburn hairs. There is a nice kink to the hairs.

THICKNESS
That is where this wig is sadly lacking. At the top, the wefts of hair are way too far apart. The lace in the cap is a very light butter colored yellow. The hair is not too thin, but it is not quite thick enough to cover hair below. Yes, this comes with a nylon cap, but it just is not comfortable with those. If you have dark hair it will definitely show the bright colored lace and elastics through the wig when the wind blows.

BANGS/STYLE
That is where this wig is just not practical unless you don't mind looking stupid for a party or Halloween. The bangs are WAY too long for anyone to wear. That usually would not be a problem, but what you will get instead of the cool light ends on the entire head is chopped bang that is bland looking and then these white cool looking ends around the head. The bangs are best cut painstakingly so that the auburn is cut way shorter (about 2/3) than the white hairs. That takes a lot of time but worth the effort. Then you have to cut them at a staggered manner.

Other than the bangs being hard to trim so you can at least function with this wig on, the overall style is fabulous. I love how it falls and looks while on the head.

ELASTIC BANDS
Inside the wig, there are elastic bands with hooks to help hold the wig on the head. You might want to take them down to the spot you like it in as the hooks have a tendency to come undone during wearing.

WHAT I WANT IN A WIG
Believe it or not, I would actually wear a wig like this with the right outfit, and not to be silly either. I prefer wigs that look authentic,, and can be worn realistically as well as for fun.

1. I have to be able to see out of it
2. I have to be able to wear it comfortably without fussing
3. I want it to not have my real hair showing
4. I want it to look realistic
5. I want it to last for quite a few wearings

DOES THIS WIG PASS THE TEST?
I am giving this wig THREE stars because it is hard to wear and see. In order to trim this in a realistic manner, I have to take a LOT of time and that takes stars off for me. I happen to love the style and coloring, so I am wiling to put the work into it, but honestly, I think it should be a bit shorter in the bangs area since it is so hard to trim and keep it looking real. Also, the wefting on the top is just a bit too widely spaced. I wish also that the cap was made with light auburn lace and elastic instead of the icy yellow colors.

THE BOTTOM LINE
If you want to wear this for fun, it will be hard to see and hard to trim and not look silly in this. It is comfortable and the style is epic, but there will be work required. You can bandana it to help, but it still will look a bit floppy unless trimmed a little bit in the bangs/fringe area. I like this, but it takes work to wear and not look silly for me.

MY RATING
THREE STARS. The trimming of the bangs is VERY time consuming since we only have one shot at it and if it is screwed up, then the wig is toast. I wish there was more hair on top and that the lace cap did not show as easily. A darker cap underneath (light auburn color) would have been much nicer with this. I will still use this, but it could have been a bit nicer with small inexpensive changes.

As a makeup artist, I am always trying to find ways to get the most mileage out of the products that I use. This bronzer had some surprises to it. Read on..

PHOTO- My photo has swatches of both color 1 and 2 which are labeled. I tried to get accurate photos colorwise and it is hard to do as the camera does not capture the nuances. When applied with a brush, the effect is MUCH lighter.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
COMPACT
The compact is a high layered cardboard with a strong hinge to it. There is no mirror and the pan inside has the product with designs pressed into it. It does not come with a brush.

WHAT IS THE COLOR LIKE?
This color is more of a bronze gold color. It is still on the cooler side, but light warmer skin tones could use this too.

TYPE OF SKIN TESTED ON?
This was tested on both MAC translation of skin tones NW 25 (which is what you see in the photos) and NC37 which is a more tan but cooler skin tone.

HOW TO APPLY?
This applies well but you have to be sure you find the right brush. A stippling brush was the best way to get a natural look from this bronzer and highlighter. It allows for subtle application so that it does not look like you have on too much. If you use too dense of a brush, it is easy to get a stripe of glow on your face that others will see and it can really look odd. You also need to get a fresh brush and blend it very well into your skin. Apply this in the backwards 3 figure on each side of your face. Imagine two 3s in a mirror image on your face with the tips and centers touching.

ANY OTHER USES?
I found that this also makes a fabulous eye shadow. I found it to be a perfect match with the other color in this series of number 2 which is a darker more rose brown color. This is a great companion to that. If this is all you have, It also makes a great eye shadow alone or with another lighter satin finish shadow or even a matte. I would not go super frosty.

HOW TO APPLY TO EYES
In terms of eyes, you can use this as a contour, all over color, or in combination with the other darker color of this Sungasm series or another set of shadows. The application is best for a lighter look to use a teardrop shaped brush. Then for a heavier look with more color, a flat eye shadow brush packing this gently into place over a good eye primer is the way to go. For a quick application, you can also use a finger to apply and blend it with a brush or your finger

ANY IRRITATION PROBLEMS?
I am VERY sensitive and did not have any problems with this product on the face or eyes.

THE BOTTOM LINE
As long as you are willing to take some time to find the right brush for the application of this, this bronzer is a pretty color especially for cooler toned skin. It is a good highlighter for darker skin tones as a highlighter, though. This is beautiful on the face, eyes, and in tandem with the other color of this bronzer too.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is a nice bronzer and I am surprised at how well it works on cooler skin tones, something that is not all that easy to find, especially in TWO colors of a collections.

I am a makeup artist. I am always finding ways to make cosmetics work for all sorts of uses to get the best look and bang for the buck. This Luminating Bronzer has some surprises up its sleeve.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
COMPACT
This comes in a heavy cardboard compact with a strong cardboard hinge on it. There is no mirror. The pan inside has printed letters and design on it. In this case, the color is number 2, the darker of the two in this collection.

WHAT COLOR IS THIS?
This bronzer is a unique color. Instead of being the usual brown or orange color so many bronzers are, this one is a rose toned base which at first seems unusual. If used on cooler toned skin, you will still see a luminzer effect but the undertone is more of a rose tan.

WHAT COLOR SKIN DID I USE THIS ON?
Right now, I tried this on two colors of skin. One was translated into MAC foundation color as NC27- a tanned color which leans toward the cooler side, and NW25 which is a cooler lighter caucasian leaning color.

EFFECTS?
Things like this have a need for you to choose the right brush. The wrong brush can make it look horrible. The right brush can make it look like a million bucks. When used with a STIPPLING brush (look that up to find out what that means), this bronzer provides the perfect luminescence and glow along with color.

You can see the cheekbones highlighted and see the spot of color, but it is subtle, and not overbearing.

If you use the dense fluffy brush like you might use to apply blush, the results border on ridiculous. It is like you have smears of bright shimmer on and it is hard to blend in well.

WHAT OTHER USES?
Interestingly, I have both color 1 and 2 of this line of Sungasm bronzers. When using this particular color 2 on the creases of the eyes, it provides a GORGEOUS natural look similar to the old J Lo type look or other natural based looks which in reality take a lot of makeup but they just don't look like it.

This put together with color 1 in this series, the two together make a great duo on the eyes. It really is amazing. It brings out the color of the eyes perfectly. In fact, I use the lighter one on the upper cheekbones for highlight/bronzer and the darker number 2 under it and blend well. The effect is subtle but beautiful.

HOW TO APPLY TO EYES
I have used good shadow brushes and my finger as well. The idea is for medium to subtle color, use a tear drop shaped shadow brush. For more intensity use a flat eye shadow brush on top of eye primer and blend once you have applied the other colors. For a quick application, I have successfully used my fingers.

DOES IT BURN ON THE EYES?
I have a terrible time with products on my eyes. They usually burn and give me trouble. This bronzer did not do that. If you are concerned, be sure to get a good eye primer that you are comfortable with and use that first on your eyes.

WHAT ABOUT DARKER SKIN TONES?
If you use this on darker skin tones, there is a good chance it could show up a bit on the ghostly side. It has to be applied very lightly and blended well a little at a time to test the best depth if you want to try it.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Not only as a gorgeous rose based bronzer highlighter, but also as a contour or all over eye shadow, this color bronzer is a great price with good performance. It is not the usual color for bronzers but it works on medium to lighter skin tones.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is a great multi purpose product for summer. It doubles as bronzer and luminzer but also as a great eye shadow.

Kenmore 27" Top-Load Washer with Triple Action Impeller and 4.8 Cubic Ft. Total Capacity, White is a very highly top rated machine by me. I will first tell you that I was a dry cleaning/laundry Inspector for half a decade, so you will know my expertise in my review of this beautiful machine. Before buying this washing machine, I owned a Whirlpool Calypso HE washer, which just died after 20 years of weekly use. The secret to keeping a machine running for 20 years- luck, use a surge protector that is made for washing machines (protects those circuit boards), run an empty load with a cup of vinegar to keep it clean inside at least once or twice a year and always load it properly with not too much soap. I do read reviews before buying anything here on Amazon and other websites and that helps greatly in my decision making.

Before I received this machine, I measured all the doorways, as our house is small and have narrow doors. The machine is a hair over 27 inches wide, and my doorways 28 inches after removing the doors. Amazon delivered it perfect- being slow and careful having only close to ½ inch on each side of the doorways. I was very happy with Amazon’s skilled delivery team. The set up takes a bit of time (I did this), as you want it as level as you can get it. I first hooked up the drain hose. There is a drain hose with clamp included, BUT, this drain hose is a very short 28 inches long, with the curved part that goes into the wash tub 23 inches long. The opening of the drain to this washer is on the back- bottom right side of this machine, 6 inches above the floor. I needed a 10 foot drain hose to go all the way behind the machine, along the side and up to the laundry tub, then into it. I ordered one here on Amazon which took a couple days. It’s perfect! So, please note- DRAIN HOSE INCLUDED IS VERY SHORT! The good part was, they included 3 metal circular clamps that worked perfect on the 10 foot hose, so I only needed to buy the hose and use one of the clamps.

I then, attached a grounding wire (our home is old), the water hoses (NOT INCLUDED) and plugged it in. Now, I adjusted the machine from the back wall (evenly on each side) to leave just enough room for the drain hose on the floor. When, I had it perfect, I marked around the machine corners on the floor with tape, so after moving it to adjust the legs, I can place it back perfectly. The legs of the machine can be adjusted on the legs- NOT the base feet on the floor, just above the base feet with a 3/4 inch wrench. You’ll need a short 2 by 4 board to hold the washer up while adjusting the legs. Check every so often with a level on the sides and top (directions in booklet), until it’s as level as you can get it. Now, turn on the water hoses, and while running your first load you can check for any leaks from the water lines and drain line.

I opened the beautiful clear lid and loaded my laundry. When you load, place items in evenly around the center (not bunched up), and as you load, VERY lightly push down (as the tub tilts easily). You do not want clothes around the center that can fall over, making the machine out of balance. You always want to see the center of the tub when finished. The tub in this washer is a huge 23 inches wide by 20 inches deep. I then added my detergent- less than you think. I had to remove the liquid-only inside cup of the detergent drawer to just use powder. I use a few tablespoons per load. And should you need to rinse clothes before washing, there is a Faucet Button! Then, I closed the lid. Push Power, select the load- I first chose Towels (for towels, sheets, socks and underthings), the cycle came up Heavy Duty and the water very warm. I can also add a variety of other things such as Extra Rinse, or change the water temperature. Once ready, I hold the Start button for a couple seconds, as it counts down to zero. The lid locks and that’s it.

I watched all the cycles with this washer and this is where I was impressed. The spraying action comes from 9 jets all around the machine. The wash basket moves in a circular motion BOTH ways if it needs more balance. The impeller action moves it back and forth. And talk about the water fill- THE WATER COVERS THE CLOTHES! It takes time to clean so well with enough water- this load took about an hour and 15 minutes. As for my regular shirts, slacks, blouses and pants. I have always put these in net bags. I have all sizes from small to really big enough for a couple pairs of pants. I learned from my Inspector job that all machines can be rough on my regular clothing, but not with net bags. They keep my clothes perfect. I used the Delicate Load and only changed the Cold water to Warm. This load took 50 minutes. When done, the machine tells you on the LCD board. When I removed my clothes, I immediately noticed they smelled so clean and looked like new. I mean bright, beautiful colors with no dinginess. The difference from this washer to other Impellers- water that covers the clothes in both wash and rinse (my old Whirlpool mainly sprayed leaving dry spots, where I saw this one cover the clothes in water completely), No lint all over the clothes (my old machine left lint always), clothes are super bright and smell super clean and it takes more time to really clean clothes. As for blankets, this machine is outstanding with it's huge capacity. Just put it around the bottom evenly, gently pushing down and then wash on Bulky. My Queen Comforters came out beautiful, bright, clean and smelling lovely.

The last thing I wanted to find out, is who made this machine and where? The model number that starts with 110 means it was made by Whirlpool. (Those that start with 417 are made by Frigidaire). Since 2017, Kenmore products have been made by other manufacturers. I was happy with this, as I’ve always liked Whirlpool. And it was made in Ohio, of course where the parts come from is another story. But being put together here in the USA also made me happy. This is a top rated machine by me, which gave me sparkling clean clothes from actually using more water. 5 STARS.

I can attest to the immediacy, and it will be with using this for greater amount of time to determine if it a repurchase or not. As I learn more, I will share more. Here is a break down of what is in it and what to expect:

BLANCHET GLAM PEARL RADIANCE CAPSULE SERUM is a supremely light weight gel serum with hint of floral scent from lavender, geranium, rose, and sandalwood. Barely detectable. A little goes a long way. This weightless serum adds a mild level of healthy sheen. Korean Beauty emphasizes healthy skin, hydrated skin, supple skin, dewy, glowing skin. It is never matte. So while you could cover this with your foundation or powder, KB is all about letting natural skin shine through. The gentle, mild barely there sheen provides more of a glass look than a shiny look. Subtle. As for the rest... The primary active ingredients are NIACINAMIDE (2%) and ADENOSINE (.04%).

NIACINAMIDE is a skin care work horse. It provides a variety of benefit to all skin types, ages, and concerns. It is a water-soluble vitamin (B3) that works with the natural substances in your skin to help improve skin barrier, fix past damage, visibly minimize enlarged pores, tighten lax pores, improve uneven skin tone, soften fine lines and wrinkles, diminish dullness, and strengthen a weakened surface. As I hone in on ingredients that pack the greatest punch, niacinamide has stood out as a must have ingredient in my skin care routine. I especially like it for its ability to brighten pigmentation. It also is one of few ingredients that work well with other ingredients without concern for contraindication or nullification. Skin care can get tricky, and this ingredient is just so easy to work with- so go ahead and use it with retinol, peptides, acids, etc. Niacinamide simply helps skin be healthy and look healthy and radiant. As with most skin care, it can take several weeks to several months of consistent use to see changes. This serum will help over time, but other ingredients provide an instant radiant glow.

ADENOSINE is a rising star in anti aging products. There are studies that demonstrate that adenosine is an effective ingredient for improving the appearance of wrinkles, in both the eye and mouth area. Interestingly, adenosine directly affects the production of type I and type III collagen in the skin by binding to A2A receptors in fibroblast cells. So if it can help boost (or at least maintain) collagen, and help collagen from breaking down (collagen is what keeps our skin plump. Compare your 45 year old face to your 18 year old face, if your face now looks "thinner" despite no losing weight, it is the decrease of collagen that has produced that look). Since adenosine has been shown to stimulate the production of collagen, applying it topically can help to prevent (and somewhat even reverse) wrinkles. *thumbs up*

I love the look of these bottles. They are cobalt blue, and really stand out from the usual amber tints. The bottle itself is well-made and sturdy. The included caps (2 were provided) are of excellent quality, with polycone inserts to maintain an air-tight, leak proof seal. The included sprayers (2 were provided) are functional, but rather cheap in terms of build quality, especially the trigger. It also comes with a tiny little funnel that is way undersized and pretty useless given the bottle volume, and a few black labels (which require a white pen, which is NOT included).

Each bottle comes in a bubble pack sleeve, but the box itself is rather thin with limited protection. These are a notch below other bottles I've received when it comes to manufacturer-provided protective packing. Still, the bottles did not break or chip in transit.

The bottles needed a good wash before use since the outside had some type of greasy-feeling film. I would have washed them regardless of their condition, but these definitely needed a good washing before use.

Taking everything into consideration I'll rate these as 4 stars. Well worth considering if you need a more colorful option than amber and don't expect to be using the sprayer much (or at all).

These clips are great!  I used to never section my hair - didn't know about it and wasn't sure of the point.  But then I realized that (1) I tended to do a good job at first and then rush though when I got tired and (2) unruly hair is easier to manage in small sections.  So, I use these clips daily to help keep my hair looking like I love myself.  Having so many is nice because I don't have to worry about losing some.  I also use them to keep my hair drying bonnet from opening up due to the air pressure.  And, I use them to hold my towel closed.  BUT, oftentimes, the silicone breaks.  So, I wanted a large quantity to help make up for this.  So, I deducted a star due to the lack of durability of the silicone - once it breaks, the hold feels much, much firmer.  I wish that there was a way to reattach it.  But, all in all, this is a great value in terms of quantity but could be better in durability.

If you're a dog owner, its practically guaranteed at some point, you will have to deal with your dog having dirty, muddy paws. Happens often with our bichon Mac. (Naturally, it recently happened right after I cleaned and mopped the house! lol)  I ordered the Mr. Ros automatic cleaner for small/medium dogs. Its very sturdy and durable, not at all flimsy.  Its roughly 8"tall  and has a removable mat with silicone bristles in the interior which is easily removable for cleaning purposes.  The bristles are very soft and not at all hard or sharp. It arrived already charged. A USB cord is included. To operate, simply add water to the washer-(2-3 cups per instructions) Liquid soap may be added as well. (I didn't use soap) Turn the washer on-it does make noise though its  not terribly loud at all-and place the dog's paw in the washer for 1-2 minutes. Dry each paw with a towel after cleaning. Mac wasn't thrilled throughout the cleaning process but he also wasn't really scared by it. My husband started to pour out the dirty water before I could stop him so you won't see much,  but you can see in my photo the water is discolored a bit following the cleaning.  If a wet towel isn't enough to clean Mac's muddy/dirty paws, my regular cleaning method is to put some lukewarm water in a small bowl , dunk each paw one at a time and use my hand to remove the dirt from his fur while submerged. Quite honestly, I really don't see much of a difference between that cleaning method and the Dr. Ros paw washer. Perhaps results vary depending on the breed of dog but for our bichon, I really don't see a  difference.
Hadn’t changed it in 2 years so I needed one.  These came on time and easy to replace so definitely be ordering them again

This is a beautiful and affordably priced facial set! The Brazilian rose quartz stones are a pale shade of pearlescent pink, and the rose gold hardware is the perfect complement to them! The rollers move silently, as promised, and they don’t seem to rust or wear out in any way. The stones are cool to the touch at room temperature, but placing them in the refrigerator (before use) ensures an ultra-chilled experience. I love that the magnetic box lid has instructions printed on the underneath side, and the soft, drawstring pouch is an added bonus! The set even comes with a informational mineral card that provides reassuring details about the quartz pieces featured. Each tool is perfectly nestled within in its own compartmentalized cutout, and the rollers definitely seem to help increase circulation and boost overall skin radiance! This would definitely make a perfect gift set for someone! I've seen so many of these jade roller/rose quartz sets and they all look the same except for the prices. This one is a good set to give as a gift because it's larger and nicer than some of the more chintzy sets. It comes with not only the usual rose quartz roller with the questionably useful Gua Sha stone (personally I found it useless for skin issues but they nevertheless include it in all these sets) but a small roller, which you almost never see anywhere. It's the perfect size for travelling and works just as well as the larger version.

However, the larger roller has spikes on one end, which I don't like at all and which they had kept the usual smooth end. It seems made for microdermabrasion which is painful to use and which I don't believe works at all for beautifying your face, only hurting it. Except for this, I like this set.

I'm impressed with this face soap. It's very thick and silky, and only a very small amount is needed to get good results. That's especially welcome to find out given the price for a pretty small bottle. It lathers up well and does a good job of cleaning without leaving my skin overly dry. It is a bit more intensive than other face soaps, so my face does feel a little 'tight' after using it. However, it's not excessive, and well worth it given how well this soap cleans if you have an oily complexation. The charcoal makes the soap dark, but it's not as jet-black as other charcoal soaps I've used. It's more of a deep gray.

The scent is also quite nice. It's a medium/light intensity and has sort of an after-shave smell to it. The scent does not linger much at all after rinsing. While I tend to prefer unscented soaps, this scent is pleasant and enjoyable.

The only con is the bottle. Getting the pump nozzle to pop up was a chore since the retaining ring the pump head screws into also rotates, making it a struggle to get the nozzle to pop up. I eventually got it working, but have noticed that the pump leaks at the stem. It's a small leak, but it adds up over a few days to make a mess on the bottle and waste soap. Given the price, the pump mechanism should have been of better quality.

One star down for the bottle issues, but otherwise, it's a very enjoyable soap to use.

We have now all been dealing with COVID for some time now and sadly have gotten used to wearing masks. At work I have to wear these types of surgical face masks as part of our PPE in the lab. I've not come across a face soap in this format -- it's a stick format, much like an antiperspirant. You rub the stick on your dry face, then use water. It's different but very easy to get used to quickly.

The soap doesn't lather all that much but it does do a good job of cleaning without drying out my face. The scent is quite nice, with the eucalyptus coming through the most. It's a medium/mild level of scent that is noticeable without being overwhelming. The scent does not linger after rinsing. The soap itself is black due to the inclusion of charcoal.

The dispensing tube is well done, with a screw base that pushes up the soap easily and evenly. It also has a screw top cover, which is a nice touch for keeping the lid affixed if you take this while traveling or use it in a gym bag.

It's an unusual but enjoyable twist on face soap. A bit pricey for the amount you get, but it's sufficiently unique to justify the cost, in my opinion. Five stars.

I'm pleased with this face scrub. It hits the right middle ground: not so coarse that you feel as if you're rubbing gravel on your face, but not so fine that there's no scrub action. This provides a good amount of scrubbing but not to the point where it's irritating. It's a medium thick cream consistency that spreads easily. Not much is needed per use.

The scent is fairly mild and while you can pick out the eucalyptus scent it's not so strong to be overwhelming, as eucalyptus can sometimes get. The scent does not linger after rinsing.

Checks all the right boxes for me for a face scrub. Five stars.

There is a lot of lotion (3.38 fluid ounces) for the $24 price tag. This lotion is creamy and very hydrating. It also absorbs quickly. Unfortunately, I am not at all crazy about the eucalyptus scent. If I loved the scent, this would have received 5 stars from me.

BTW, this is good for a man or a woman despite what the title says. My boyfriend's face has been really dry and flaky lately and I needed to get something he would use and something that would work. This lotion is lightweight, but very moisturizing. It has a light pleasant scent that isn't too overpowering and dissipates pretty quickly. I appreciate that the flaky skin and dryness went away too!

I love this back scrubber, and hung it in my shower as soon as I could. It is quite long with handles, and each side has a different size brush. The sponge on a rope is a nice bonus. I currently have a back brush with a handle, and it does the job but not as well as this product. My back hasn't felt so clean in a long while. I admit I also use it to scratch my back while in the shower, so relaxing and it doesn't have any points to scratch me.
This product is worth every penny of $11.99. I recently started using one of these with loofa on it. It works for me, even if loofa does take a while to break in. However, it also absorbs quite a bit of soap. I like this one much better.

I was a little hesitant to order it. How would silicone feel against my back? It turns out that it feels fine and works well. I like that it needs much less soap since it doesn't absorb it. Instead of spreading it all over the thing - I like the side with little bristles like a brush - all you need is to put some in the center. Moving the brush over your back spreads the soap out nicely and does the job without a lot of waste. It squeaks a bit on un-soaped skin, but that's pretty easy to get over and doesn't last long. It was just a surprise, initially. It feels like a gentle scrub, and that's the important part. It also rinses off easily and dries quickly, an important point here in our humid climate. The interior relative humidity in our house hovers around 55% in the summer, so things can get moldy fast. That's what usually happens if a loofa or any other kind of absorbent surface isn't dried properly. I just hang this up on the thoughtfully provided suction hooks and forget about it. It's great, and I'm really glad I gave this a try! It's long enough to get around your back and sturdy enough to not flip around when you are scrubbing your back. It has a scrubby side and a massaging nubby side. They both feel great on your skin. It came with a little natural sponge and several sticker hangers for in the shower that come in handy to help them dry better.

The on/off switch as at the bottom of the appliance and it's very easy to depress.  If you need an ice maker and are prepared to defrost this every four to six weeks, it seems to be a good product. This ice maker is about the size of a dorm refrigerator and it's a great option for a basement bar type situation or health care need.

I have been trying, for well over 30 years, to get a curling iron that actually did what it was supposed to – curl my hair.

Hot curlers – no good results

Curling Irons (¼, ½) – no good results

Wrap-Around Fabric Curlers – nothing there

I saw this and thought it couldn’t fail. Simple to use – plug in, turn on, heat up, section hair, and use – put hair in, count down.

Works in theory, fails in execution. First up – there is NO heat seating guide for SAFE curling. THIS DEVICE IS CELSIUS (C) ONLY, NO FARENHEIT (F) OPTION. Google is strongly needed here.

According to Redken: “For those with fine or thin hair, keep your iron set below 200 (so below 100°C on this device) degrees Fahrenheit. Any higher and your strands may burn. For those with coarse or thicker hair, have your curling iron set between 200 degrees and 300 degrees (148.9°C or on this device 150) Fahrenheit for optimal curls” [9 Curling Iron Secrets You Need to Know About/Redken]

Using that, as well as Glamour’s 8-10 second rule [How to Curl Your Hair Correctly: 7 Mistakes to Avoid – Glamour; “Drill it into your brain: You should hold an iron on your hair for eight to 10 seconds max”], along with using thinner groups of hair – I should have SOME wave. Nope. I even went 25 seconds. Nothing.

As my hair has become a bit thinner, has been color treated, and exposed to SO much – I wasn’t about to turn this up hotter.

The curler is designed much like a crimper, but the “width” can make it difficult to handle, especially by yourself. There is a “guard” which heats up as well and it is easy to burn yourself.

It wins with innovative idea as well as the digital temp gauge. Also, it does heat up SUPER fast, as well as cool down just as fast when lowering the temp.

For use by myself – this is a two star deal. Perhaps if someone else were around it might be easier, but this definitely did not work well.

This is a gommage!!! The most gentle of all the physical exfoliation out there. If you haven't tried it, I highly recommend. I also highly recommend anything by Easydew. Good stuff! Know that this is meant to clump! Not supposed to have lather or creaminess. I had looked at the ingredients and some of the description and I suspected a gommage. The directions on box say to use on wet face and that it will lather. It doesn't. There is some clumps, but not as much as if it were used on a dry face, which is what is expected from a gommage. We want glorious clumps! For best results use on a clean dry face, not a wet face. I have tried it both ways, definitely use on dry face. Works but not as good on wet face.

So use a generous amount. Just pat it in all over. Let it sit a moment, then massage it in in gentle circular motion. As you do so, small clumps will form. This is a combination of product and grime and dead skin cells. Basically, a "gommage" is like an eraser on a pencil, and your skin is paper. The graphite marks are dirt and dead skin cells. The product once applied is like that eraser-- it is removing those "marks". What happens when you use an erase? You start to see balled up pieces of eraser mixed with the graphite/pencil marks. That is more or less what is happening here. Those balled up pieces are a mix of product, dirt, and cells. Rinse, and carry on with rest of your routine. It is a very gentle "peel". And quite effective. But less so when used on wet skin-- the ingredients just can't grab the gunk on face as well. I'm surprised there is such a discrepancy in instructions.

Instructions on container:
"How to use:
Apply desired amount of peeling gel and work into a rich lather by wet hands.
Gently cleanse by massaging thoroughly over face in circles, avoiding eye contour.
Rinse off with lukewarm water."

But the pictures clearly show what is expected--balled up bits/clumps.

SO, it it may be a matter of terminology/language. Easydew has some wonderful products, and this is a good product that I will use maybe 2x a week. I love how smooth my skin feels and that it doesnt feel parched afterward.

The bottle and texture is very much like a hair mousse or shaving cream, but is a wash for the body. Instead of a pump or squeeze bottle, this comes out though as pressure aerosol - also just like a mousse or shaving cream. The ingredients necessary to make this happen are Butane and Propane. They are aerosol propellents. If you have ever used mousse, hair spray, various perfumes/body sprays, air fresheners, aerosol deodorants, or shaving cream,etc.. then you are already familiar with these ingredients. They are generally recognized as safe, and are used in small, diluted quantities in skin care. Fun fact, "These ingredients are used in cosmetics and personal care products as a replacements for chlorofluorocarbons, or CFC propellants, some of which have been shown to have negative effects on the environment". I'm not a big fan of slathering my body with butane, propane, or isobutane, but I understand their use in this type of medium. So it's up to you to decide.

This company does have non aerosol body wash available too..

I thought these were bath bombs when I ordered them. However, that is not what this is at all. There are 10 tiny balls of compressed flowers wrapped in various colored foils. They can be used as a tea, which is what I use them for, or they can be put in a bath. I have no idea how anyone would use this for baking as per the Amazon title.

Nevertheless, all but the purple and red balls have a purely vegetal scent. The purple and red smell flowery. I have used tea balls before and never cared for them but did like how most stayed together. However, these balls expand into many little flower particles that float in the water. If one were to put this in a bath, it would clog the drain unless the flower debris was scooped out with a skimmer.  I used the blue ball to brew into a tea and it was tasteless. I also had to use a strainer and remove the lid on my pot to keep the spout from clogging.

Besides the mess and lackluster flavor, there are absolutely no brewing instructions, no information on what tea ball is what flower.  The Amazon site has a list of the flower and the balls but does not show the foil color. It is almost impossible to reconcile that list with what is in front of me.

Shame on the vendor for not creating an insert or package label that says what is inside and which tea ball is what flower. I personally do not care for this at all and will probably throw this in the garbage.

This is not worth it to me at any price. It is certainly not a bath bomb, I can't see how it can be used for baking, and as a tea it is tasteless and messy. There is no fragrance, so its use as a bath bomb would be for romantic or ambiance purposes only.

At the current price of $9.88 for 10 balls it comes to almost $1 per tea ball.

First, I will say these oils seem fine. They work well together or apart, mixed into other skincare products or alone. I use these types of oils to make my own facial oil mix or to add to my moisturizer.
The thing I absolutely hate that companies do to try to sell their products is to say things that aren't true. The USDA does not certify oils - food, cosmetic, or otherwise. The fact that the bottle says this product is USDA certified on one side, and the other side says not intended for ingestion should speak volumes. The USDA certifies and regulates the welfare and production of food products; meaning products that you ingest. So, why on earth would they certify a product you cannot ingest? The bottle also makes outright claims of known cures from using these oils. There is no disclaimer on either bottle that states that these claims have not been approved or proven by the FDA, or whatever the disclaimer is that is mandatory. There are ingredients listed, one ingredient for each product, the oil, and that's it. Nothing tells how these oils were extracted. Therefore, we do not know if they are refined or unrefined. They probably don't know either. So you see, therein lies the lies and deception.
These oils would be much better if they weren't tied to lies. Because you know what they say about lies... if you tell one you have to tell more to keep up with the first one. Is what they say in the bottle really what's in the bottle? Are they pure oils or mixed with a lesser oil? Oils are greasy. If they are unrefined, why aren't they greasy? When you refine oils, you take away a lot of their natural properties and their nutritive value, is that why they aren't greasy? Because of the lies and lack of important information, I really don't know for sure what these oils are.
Because of the deceptive practices and claims made, I would not recommend these or any of their other oils. You get 2 massive bottles of oil, one with sweet almond oil and the other with coconut oil. For each bottle they supply you with a pump dispenser which is great. It makes it so much easier to dispense the oil without making a mess to be honest. Both oils are claimed to be organic which is nice. This will run you $25 which in my eyes is a good deal.

The oils themselves were pretty much fragrance-free which was a bit disappointing to me, but makes sense since these are often used as carrier oils. When you use this they are pretty lightweight and absorb quickly. I found they do leave the skin a bit greasy, but that is not a surprise since these are oils. That feeling does go away within about 15 minutes or so, so not too bad. All in all a good deal Great set of oils that are great to use as is or when making other products. You can remove the ice cubes and place them in a freezer, but the ice cubes are wet so when you place the cubes into the freezer they will freeze together in a clump. It’s best to turn this icemaker off before you go to bed, or when you are leaving the office, and not let it run when no one is there to use or remove the ice. Otherwise, as stated above, the eye simply melts in the process of refreezing continues again and again.

Since I basically am home 24/7, I've invested in air quality enhancements around our home and tools to measure our rooms.

What this does right:
The display is spot on. Clear, legible, easy to see without glasses, not blinding at night, etc...
Has a clock--I love that I can see the time easily at night without resorting to a bright phone
The size is right
Power--using 5v USB opens up many options

What could be better:
No connectivity to the larger Acurite ecosystem--using their other connect indoor and outdoor sensors, this feels disconnected with no ability to connect to app, track history, send notifications.
Since it's lacks the above, I'd tend to want to use this around the house, and this lacks a built in battery powered option. It's not hard to connect to a power pack, but I wish I could charge up or add AA. The primary purpose of this AcuRite Indoor Air Quality Monitor is an alert to turn on the humidifier for sensitive family members. It's dimmable and legible. The sampling rate and screen update are appropriate.

Depending on your use, this monitor measures @PM2.5. It's an appropriate indoor green/yellow/red light monitor. @PM2.5 ≤ 12µ = green light. Yellow light between 13-35. >35? Deepening shades of red ... until you can't see color, then like-2000 years in the future, some kid will be digging a hole and strike a void, someone will pour plaster of Paris in the void and you'll live in fame, slain by flaming hot particles just like Pompeii. @PM2.5 the results are comparable to the Air Quality Index (AQI) as locally reported by NOAA.

Relative humidity (RH%) is heuristically linked to PM2.5. The higher the RH%, the lower the PM2.5. The lower the RH%, the higher the PM2.5 reading. I’ve noticed that an interior RH% ≈ 50% displays 1-5 ppm.

As a note to ‘bunny suit’ people, PM2.5 is not the metric for comparisons to ISO cleanroom levels. This monitor might suggest 1-5 ppm, but, my living room is NOT class 10 ... given rugs, etc, it can't be made to get to class 100,000.

Twenty years ago, this sensor was a high-$ industrial proposition and hardly for home use. However, Acurite has packaged a bundle of technology here to deliver excellent value for money.

When I opened this package, I had no idea what I was looking at. Inside the Amazon packaging bag was another bag, a plastic bag with a bubble wrap lining and a ziplock type zipper. Upon further investigation, I discovered it was the Play Pretend brand of under eye cream. Yes, the Amazon product page does state the the cream comes in a syringe-like tube, and yes, it does state that it comes with a skincare travel bag, this wasn’t what I had envisioned.
On to the product…
Once I figured out how to open and operate the syringe (hint: remove the large, clear cap, remove the white tip, turn the plunger to unlock) to dispense the under eye cream, I applied some to my face. The scent is strong, like cucumber with an underlying perfume smell. Not unpleasant, but kind of strong for me, someone who is overly sensitive to scents. My problem, I know, and most people will probably really enjoy the scent. The cream is white, smooth, goes on evenly and is absorbed quickly. There is a bit of a cooling sensation which I found pleasant.

The travel bag seems unnecessary to me. It’s really not much more than a heavy ziplock bag lined with bubble wrap with a large logo reading “Skin Set Go.” If someone needs a bag, great, but I have several and I don’t think I’ll be using this one.

According to the company’s website, Skin Care Go products are made in the USA in small batches. Good. A lot of natural ingredients go into the product, which I like, but the complete list of ingredients from the company’s website is as follows:

Water (Aqua), Carthamus Tinctorius Seed Oil, Polyacrylate-13, Glycerin, Propylene Glycol, Polyisobutene, Squalane, Sodium Hyaluronate, Acetyl Hexapeptide-8, Cucumis Sativus (Cucumber) Fruit Extract, Retinyl Palmitate, Tocopherol, Palmitoyl Tripeptide-1, Palmitoyl Tetrapeptide-7, Butylene Glycol, Polysorbate 20, Acetyl Octapeptide-3, Caprylyl Glycol, Potassium Sorbate, Phenoxyethanol, Ethylhexylglycerin, Fragrance, Yellow 5 (CI 19140), Blue 1 (CI 42090).

The final verdict:
The product is nice, and while I’d personally prefer something less heavily scented, I like the way the cream works and what it does for my skin. It’s very hydrating and brightening, with nothing that irritated my skin. I understand the idea behind the syringe dispenser: it’s unique, it’s fun, it’s memorable. However, there’s a ton of plastic used that isn’t necessary, and with the design, I don’t know how I’ll know when the tube is nearing empty.
Overall, this is a good product, does what it says it does, and if you’re looking for something a little unusual, give it a try. Houseboats - boats in general - require different setups.  Much like RVs, actually.  But the thing about that kind of living is that kitchen areas are small and require that things be moveable/storeable.  To get to the point, I cooked on both radiant and induction plates with two burners each so I did have a full-size stovetop, but they were easier to store when I needed the countertop for other things.  Of the two cooking surfaces, I did find radiant cooktops to be a bit more versatile as induction requires that the utensil have a metal bottom so that the heat reaction would occur.  Not that induction is bad, but it does require more thought in the preparation.  Radiant heat cooktops are the better part of electric cooking - no coils that are exposed, a flat surface that stays that way (I have had a couple of stove tops that one coiled burner was slightly bent up) and is easy to clean.  This surface was fairly easy to install - the electrician was here for right at 30 minutes as I had already removed my traditional oven/stove and replaced it with a Goodwill lower kitchen cabinet.  The back of the cabinet was removed, the top I had already cut to fit this drop in unit and that's exactly what I did and then let the electrician do his part to get this wired.  Now, if you are wondering what I will be doing without an oven that went out the door with the traditional stove, I have a multi-use full size microwave that also air fries, bakes, and broils.  I can fit two full size cookie sheets in my microwave unit and yes, I can cook with metal when using air fry, bake or broil.  Back to the radiant heat cooktop - electrician gone, I had been waiting to try it out and grabbed a smaller skillet, a frozen burger and got to it!  Radiant heat doesn't cook faster or better if that's what you think, but it works great and my burger was finished in a short time.  The burner does take time to cool down, but that's more or less a given with most electric heating.  That is probably the biggest plus of induction over radiant cooking, in how it cools down; however, I am more than pleased with how this radiant heat cooktop is truly and completely flat.  No knobs to turn/twist!  The four burners have a touch-sensitive section in the front to pick which one you want to use and also, two are 1200 watt and two are 1800 watt so you have higher power for stir frying or the like.  One last thing - as I mentioned, I had an electrician wire this cooktop because it had to be tied to a 220 breaker/30 amp load in my home's circuit box.  Being that I'm not comfortable working with electric lines, best to pay someone who knows what they are doing, right?  So, bottom line is, if you are ready to upgrade your kitchen, this radiant heat flat cooktop would be a wonderful addition  to your kitchen.

This is a fine performing bullet ice machine. The controls are easy to use, it works quickly, and ejects the ice neatly and properly each time. But, as with any bullet ice machine, the ice itself is not of ideal quality. It's cloudy and melts quicker than clear ice. Clear ice machines do cost a fair amount more (the Frigidaire model is probably the least expensive one but it costs nearly twice as much as this) but the ice quality is better. Still, for the price, this is a good performer in the bullet ice category.

The overall fit and finish is decent. The gearing for the ice ejection is all plastic, but that's to be expected for the price. The manual is pretty poor, but it's not hard to figure out how to use the machine. Operating sounds are hushed (other than the loud bang the ice makes when it is ejected and hits the catch container). It has a self-cleaning function but I can't tell what it actually cleans -- it seems to just recirculate the water a few times. I imagine it is cleaning (or attempting to clean) hard water deposits on the innards of the machine, but can't be sure.

There's a drain plug which is handy for getting rid of the water when you're done with the machine. It is located on the bottom, so you have to position the machine so the front half is hanging over a sink so it can drain without making a mess. Not the most convenient place for a drain plug, but it works.

Although this has all the limitations of other bullet ice machines, it works well and is easy to use. For the price it's a five star performer. If you are willing to spend a bit more, however, it's worth looking at clear ice machines since the ice quality is better.

I am very pleased with my experience using the Feminine Cleansing Wash. This is very easy to use in the shower as it has a hand pump. This foaming cleanser genuinely provides an oil-free approach to daily acne control. I like that it contains botanical extracts, and it seems to provide a gentle, yet thorough, clean! It’s nicely packaged, affordably priced, has a pleasant scent, a 2+ year shelf life, and it always leaves my skin feeling nourished, soft, and smooth. I’d recommend it to others without hesitation! I think a lot of us want an easier way to remove hair. Shaving, especially for a bigger girl like me, is not that easy. It’s worse when you have long legs, short arms.

It’s bad when you have certain chin hairs (thankfully not that much it isn’t manageable another way).

I tried some sugar wax kit back about 20+ years ago. That was a NIGHTMARE! It was supposedly edible. I think you microwaved the container, spread it on, let it cool, used a paper strip (supplied) to remove the hair. It didn’t work and stung.

I then moved to a hair removal cream, that partially worked.

After that? Back to the hold stand-by –> shave foam/cream and a razor. For my main body parts, that’s always worked. Tough “chin” hairs –> using a tweezer work. No, the dermaplaning tool didn’t work on them.

I got a wax warmer, so I thought all beads/beans were equal.

These came with ZERO instructions, and the after spray bottle was busted. The warmer kit at least had some. And, my warmer kit had specially made, disposable “cups”.

These beads/beans, in a smaller cup, took over 90 minute to melt. And, the warmer was on 180°(F).

I tried a small amount on my arm. The wax was sticky, not liquidy, and it cooled almost as soon as it hit my skin.

I let it sit there for a few minutes (over 5), and peeled the max off. It didn’t hurt, sting, or cause redness – then again …

THE HAIR WAS STILL THERE

Okay, so my hair on my arm is a little thin. But, if this removes thick hair, shouldn’t it remove thinner hair?

I found another patch, got some warm wax – tried it again. Nope. Tried legs, arms, and under my chin. Nothing. Then again, I see I'm not the only one experiencing issues with these beads/beans.

I may have gotten a bad batch. But, I definitely wouldn’t get these again.

When I got my Keurig in late 2012, I thought it was the BEST coffee maker I ever bought. But, not only does those K-Cups get expensive, but they’re also not too good for the environment.

Don’t get me wrong, I’m not a NO PLASTIC EVER kind of person. I’m not a tree hugger. I’m also not “hey let’s create a boatload of waste” either. I do what I can, where I can, when I can to reduce my imprint.

As a result, along with my Keurig, I purchased a reusable cup. At that time it was the “PERFECT POD” one, and I also got their filters. And, they were pretty affordable. Sometimes hard to find.

I’m always on the lookout for a GREAT deal. Seeing these, I thought I would try them.

One thing I should’ve noticed and didn’t, and this is 100% on me, they don’t have a “lid”. If you want to know what I mean, check out my pictures. The white filters are PERFECT POD, the unbleached ones are this product.

Notice the white filter as a “lid”. This is quite useful when putting the ground in. Without the lid to cover them, they tend to fall out of the reusable cup whether the filter is FULL or not. This can lead to some grounds in the machine, your cup, and makes the top of the filter nasty to clean. The white filter with the lid prevents that entirely.

These are not easy to store or take out of the package. ALL 600 FILTERS are in ONE bag. NO individual bags to take out and store the rest until needed. One has to open the WHOLE BOX, WHOLE BAG, to get one (1) filter. I decided to grab a “group” of filters and store them in another bag.

Do these work? Aside from those issues, yes. There is no difference in the taste of the coffee. Then again I usually chill it then mix with chocolate milk for a mocha.

Whether one wants to buy these depends on whether they want to clean the K-Cup EVERY SINGLE CUP (thankfully I do have two reusable cups), and do they want to open the box and bag for one (1) filter.

Given the filter’s design -1 star; packaging -1 star.

I ended up keeping an infrared thermometer close to measure the heat and the one thing I would change on this oven. There are pros and cons to the Tirtyl Hand Soap Sheet Variety Pack. I found it difficult to get a decent lather from the sheets, even when using 2 or 3 at a time. This makes them less than ideal for bathing. However, I did get them to do a great job for cleaning just my hands. I would suggest them for cleaning hands while on the go. The scent is very light when added to water. A tin is included, which is a bit more durable than the paper envelopes. The tin slides open, matchbox style. I would recommend using the tin as it will withstand being transported in a pocket, purse or bag better than the paper envelopes. If you anticipate being exposed to rain, I would suggest to place the tin and/or envelopes into a plastic bag. Using water and friction is superior to using hand sanitizer, and with the soap sheets you will be able to maintain much cleaner hands while out and about.

If you are looking for a portable soap for bathing, I would still suggest to use bar soap wrapped in wax paper inside a plastic bag. If you are in situations where you need to wash hands without soap provided, these are ideal for that need. I would recommend the soap sheets as they are easy to transport and cost effective for hand washing. I hope you find my experience helpful and kindly will click the button below. As most have said here – these are great for travel, especially when you can’t find soap around but have water. Though I wouldn’t carry a bar of soap, I have used “travel” size body wash as a hand soap. If it cleans the body, should clean the hands, right?

Anyway …

The metal container I got was dented, but that is okay as I don’t intend to travel where I won’t have soap. So, I’m using these at my bathroom sink.

LET ME STATE THIS AS A WARNING: HANDS MUST BE DRY BEFORE GRABBING A SOAP SHEET.

I know all caps is yelling, but trust me – it is for a VERY GOOD reason. As one reviewer said, even a drop of water can damage these.

Basically I grab a one with dry hands, hold it in palm, turn water on, let it dissolve. Good lather, I don’t really smell a “scent”, hands wash clean. They don’t dry out, but I do use a moisturizing sanitizer, and hand lotion after.

I wouldn’t say these go years – if you’re like me and using them as an alternative to other hand soaps to preserve waste, they might last about a month (8 washes per day, 30 days). If only as travel backup – they might last a few years. Again, it depends on how they’re used.

I personally find them a bit on the pricey side at almost $10 before tax. That’s just me.

I do have other soaps, and these should last me a while. I would not recommend them as a body wash. As opposed to carrying a bar of soap, try a travel container with body wash. Just my suggestion. There are three packages of wafer thin sheets of soap in 80 sheets each pack. The wafers are attached in the center but pull apart easily. There is also a sliding top tin supplied that will hole 80 sheets. Be careful not to get them wet as even a drop of water causes them to dissolve. When I washed my hands with one sheet, it created a nice lather and left my hands clean. I do not feel that it was moisturizing as claimed. Also, even though there are three wonderful fragrances (lavender & aloe, bergamot & ylang ylang, and jasmine & patchouli) that smell great as a whole 80 sheets, that fragrance does not come through on the hands because the soap is too thin to leave any fragrance behind.

The current price of $13.95 comes to $.06 cents per sheet. I consider these perfect for when using a public restroom that has water but no soap. It is also great for camping or any place where portability is paramount without carrying a full wet bar of soap in a container.

We have had to buy our own ice for a while now. It was not too bad of a problem, but when things are closed around a lot, we began to wish we had an ice maker. Our refrigerator did not have the capacity for making ice and ice trays took up too much room and got tipped over too easily from careless kids. This, however, has changed all of that.

SIZE
The size of this unit is perfect if you want to have an ice maker but you don't have a lot of room. You will have to be sure to have clearance around it, however, as it won't fit in a tight space. It needs room for air to vent on the back and side.

PHOTO
In the photos I posted, I put a bottle of Pelligrino next to this unit so you can see how big it is. That is the larger Pelligrino glass bottle, not the small plastic ones.

ICE
The ice that is made from this can be smaller or larger. I picked the larger ones which also fit in most of our water bottles- a BIG plus. Smaller ones will fit in smaller bottle openings if you happen to have them.

WARNING
After reading through the instructions, I want to mention that you will want to probably use DISTILLED water for making ice in this. We have high lime content and in the past machines that recommend being cautious of lime build up even got build up that was hard to clean using our water FILTERED.

I have a few machines we have used distilled for and they have never had issues. We are using distilled with this as well.

DOES IT KEEP ICE COLD?
This keeps ice cold until you use it. It will make ice until it is full and then stop. Once it needs to be filled it will tell you that too.

QUIET?
This is very quiet compared to others I have heard.

IS IT FAST?
We got ice from this in about 7 minutes but it was only enough for one large glass. To get a larger load it took about an hour.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a fantastic little ice machine. The family is happy to have ice and not have to buy bagged ice and cram it in the storage freezer downstairs. As long as we use distilled water, I hope to not have any long range problems.

INSTRUCTIONS
Make sure to read instructions thoroughly as if you plan to not use this all of the time, you have to go through certain steps prior to storing it.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS so far. This is a big hit this summer. I am really happy to have this. It has made it so much easier to have our own ice when we want instead of realizing it is gone and have to go to the store when someone uses it up and says nothing.

These small icemakers are nice, as long as you understand exactly what it is that you are getting and exactly what it can and cannot do. For example, this icemaker cannot keep the ice frozen. So the ice cubes are made… Placed into a basket… And then you either remove them and use them or place them into your own freezer. Otherwise the ice simply melts and then will be refrozen.

The listing shows that this icemaker can make up to 33 pounds of ice per day. That is a bit of a misnomer, because the only way it can do that is if you constantly remove the ice day and night. So if this icemaker is in a location where there are people there around-the-clock, then yes it can make up to 33 pounds per day. As long as the ice is constantly being removed. But if you are at home, and using it simply for your family, then of course while you are sleeping you are not going to be removing the ice. One very nice thing that this particular model has that many others do not is the option to use a timer so that it will start and stop when you wanted to and not continue to make ice when you don’t need it to, like when you are sleeping.

This icemaker is made in China and being sold by Chinese company on Amazon. Overall, this is a nicely designed, good performing ice maker. It makes bullet type ice (the type of ice that has a hole in the base) rather than cube ice. As with any bullet ice maker, the ice is rather cloudy instead of clear. But, the ice from this is a bit more clear than other bullet ice makers I've tried. Not a lot, but it's noticeable.

Bullet ice tends to melt quicker and doesn't look as nice as cube ice. But bullet ice makers are not as expensive as cube ice makers, and I've found that bullet ice works fine. Put it in a drink and the drink gets cold. That's pretty much all I expect from ice.

The build quality feels solid. The controls are well laid out and simple to use. It has a very large LED timer readout that, while it looks nice, doesn't really add much to the functionality of the machine. It offers two ice sizes but there's not a huge difference between the "small" and "large" cubes. Since bullet ice melts quicker I always use the large size option.

It has a self-clean function but it's not a replacement for a good cleaning every so often with diluted vinegar, especially prior to storing the machine. Operating sounds are very hushed. You can hear it, but can easily have a conversation in a normal voice standing right next to it. The flaps that move the ice into the bin operate almost silently (other than the sound of the ice dropping in). It's not all that much of an energy hog, using 120W of power.

The first batch of ice takes about 9 minutes; subsequent batches are a minute or two quicker.

I like that it has the drain plug on the bottom rather than the lower side. It makes it easier to empty out the leftover water. Just move the machine so the drain plug is over the sink, pop the plug and let it drain. You don't have to hold the machine while it's draining, unlike some other models.

The only feature I didn't test is the timer (you can set it to start at a certain time). I can't envision ever needing such a feature. It does shut off automatically if the water level gets low or the collection bin is full, so you don't need to watch it even without using the timer.

The only con is the price. There are other similar bullet ice makers that are just a tad smaller but cost notably less. This is not priced outrageously, but it's not a bargain either.

4.5 stars (half star down due to the value issue). I'll round up to 5 since it works well, feels well-made, makes ice pretty quickly, is quiet, and is easy to maintain.

1) It is NOT a freezer. Once it makes the ice, the manual says to remove it to a freezer. Otherwise it just melts. It does insulate fairly well, though. I would put it on par with an average cooler.

6) I thought there was a light in it but there is not. That's an aesthetic thing to me and probably wouldn't bother most people.

Also, when I originally purchased it, it said it wouldn't ship until November but it shipped in less than a week.

If I have a choice between a plain headband and a unicorn headband, well, I’m picking the unicorn headband every time!

I'm a decent sized guy and lift things around the house often but this things still about more than I can carry myself! I recommend using a dolly and then two people to hoist it up to where it's going. Then you need to run the drain hose to a sink drain or a big 5 gallon bucket would work (just make sure you have the hose secure or it could flop out and drain in the floor) Then you can hook this up to a sink or you can fill it's tank. I filled it's tank completely as I want to go that route and I loaded it up. Once the thing started running, I filled the tank all the way up again and it didn't have to be filled again for the whole wash cycle so it's pretty convenient. I think it'd be able to do everything on one full tank.

SO this is a smaller dishwasher and one level so you could fit one large pot and a couple cups maybe. But if you're doing little things- you can still fit a few things! It took it about an hour to run it's regular cycle and then it'd run it's fan for an hour drying it and pop open automatically when it's done. I just opened the door once it was done and let it all air dry though- no sense in having it dry things if you're not in a hurry.

Some things I love about this are: the UV light while drying (never seen that in a dishwasher!), it's very quiet- you could run it in an apartment at night without it being too loud, it cleans just as good as my full sized expensive $1100 dishwasher did! I had some dishes that hadn't been cleaned for a couple weeks because I was sick and I threw them in and they came out spotless! A couple pieces of silverware had a tiny bit of food residue but that happens with most dishwashers so no biggie- just sponge cleaned it off and rinsed it in seconds.

This thing would absolutely be great for an RV, tiny home, or just on the counter of a rental. On the rental- I'd check with the landlord first as some don't want you using a washer or dishwasher due to potential water leaks. But if it's allowed- get this thing, you will love it!! I truly never thought these mini dishwashers would clean so well but they do! Cleaning them is much easier than a full size too- it's super easy to pull the screen out and clean it!

No complaints or improvements that I can think of at all! It's heavy but it does the job so I'm fine with that! Though this is listed as “Mini”. . . I would call it “Small”, but not “Mini”. It has a weight of 30#. This is not the sort of item you’ll want to (or be able to) put away and take-out frequently. You’ll need enough counter space. So you certainly need to consider if you’re willing to give-up quite a bit of counter space for this small dishwasher. . .as opposed to washing by hand.

This small dishwasher has a wand both on the bottom and the top. At first I thought it was only on the bottom. . . but. . .that’s not the case. . . and I’m happy about that. Also, this small dishwasher heats the water. So you add cold water and then the dishwasher will heat it to the appropriate temperature.

It can hold some rather large items. Coffee carafe… Blender… And so on. But it certainly not for pots and pans.

If you scroll down below the product information… You will see product guides and documents. Right under that is a link to the manual for this small dishwasher. You might want to have a look at it before purchasing. Though the “normal” cycle takes 130 minutes, the “rapid” cycle takes forty minutes. So as long as you rinse off your items beforehand, you can probably get by with the “rapid” cycle.

I also like the fact that you can use this to steam baby bottles as well as wash fruit. Though the video shows that washing strawberries, the instruction show that it is for hard fruit only.

This small dishwasher is made in China. Some key points about the product
- only uses 5 liters or 1.3 gallons of water per load
- a size comparison is slightly larger than a large countertop oven
- takes 2 hours to do a "normal" wash
- takes regular dishwasher liquid or powder (I do not recommend pods since they are made for use in full sized machines)

What I like about the product
- great size for a small family
- uses less water (5 liters or 1.3 gallons) than it would to handwash the dishes!
- does not need to be hooked up to a water source: fill it with 5 liters of water and a bucket/sink to drain
- we have a full size dishwasher but I don't run it very often and use it more for a drying rack.. we are only a family of 4 and it takes about 2 weeks for us to fill up the dishwasher but there are things I need washed frequently such as toddler sippy cup, coffee cup, etc .. so this is nice to have as a busy mom that has to do a small amount of dishes everyday.
- different settings for your needs: normal wash, wash fruit, etc...
- easy to use
- does not make much noise/pretty quiet

Cons:
- larger/ bulkier than expected
- all of our counters have cabinets above them so it didn't end up fitting anywhere in our kitchen
- had some trouble adding silverware: I had to put knives horizontally in washer because they would just slide right through or were too tall to fit in the washer.
- had a hard time finding somewhere I could put/store it since [like I mentioned before] all my counters have cabinets above them. You need to be able to put it somewhere that is a large surface to place it on, that is also by a 3 pronged outlet, plus be able to drain it somewhere (sink/bucket). I ended up running our first load while it was on top of my clothes dryer but cannot keep it there because it is blocking my laundry cabinet.
- if you don't keep it in a permanent spot you will have to pick it up and move it to use it and it's pretty heavy/bulky to do that.
- drain hose has a mind of its own.. I recommend giving it some time to straighten out and unravel because it kept wanted to go back to the shape it was stored and the suction cup was basically no help with that..

Overall I'd say this is definitely convenient to have it's just a matter of figuring out if you have the correct space for it - and if you do it's a lovely and handy machine to have!

This ice machine does what it says it does; it makes ice, and it dispenses hot and cold water. It does have a few flaws, though.

First, it gives you indication as to how much ice is left. It will tell you when it's full, and indicate when it snot full. But it can be 95% full or 2% full, and the only way you will know when it's empty is when it stops dispensing ice. You can't look inside because there is no way to open it and look.

The ice is on the soft, wet side. It's not as cold as it could be; it's close to melting. This makes it soft for chewing, but it melts easily and waters down drinks quickly.

The machine is pretty noisy while it's making ice.

The ice has a plastic-like chemical taste to it even after running a couple of gallons of water through it. The instruction said that it should take several quarts of water to get all the dust and flavor out, so this may yet pass in time, but it's pretty strong and unpleasant.

Other than these issues, well, it is indeed an ice machine. It's far from perfect, but it makes ice pretty quickly and it can provide about 5 glasses full of ice at maximum capacity.

Christmas present, so I hope it works as expected ratings were good and has a auto fill which GE didn’t. This ice maker is easy to use. It is fairly quiet and very efficient. It makes nugget ice. I vacillated between getting a four burner flat cooktop induction cooktop and a gas cooktop as I have always preferred gas over electric cooktops for the ease of controlling temperatures and when it is turned off, it's off.  Regular electric burners have to cool down which is what I really dislike.  Induction doesn't require the same cool down, but it also requires that all cookware used be compatible.  That's the main reason I went with gas - it is, for me, the most versatile for cooking with whichever pot I may be using. This particular cooktop is EXCELLENT! I don't have to look for the timer (in my everything drawer so you know what that's like!) since it's right there on the cooktop.  Very sleek-looking and easy to clean, cooks just perfectly with the ability to dial in the heat you want and when you turn it off, it's off.  That's what makes this perfect for me! We recently moved to a new home in Florida. Prior to moving here I had decided to install a whole house dehumidifier. After installing it I wanted to be able to monitor the temperature and humidity levels throughout my house - I have done this using a few different methods, one of which is this set.

These simple small devices are easy to read and even easier to operate - just pull the tab and use.

My only complaint is 2 of the 10 in this set did not work out of the box. At this price it really is still reasonable for 8 units but not as great as for 10.

I have found these units work well, the batteries last a long time and the price is reasonable. While I wish all 10 of the units worked it still is a good set that I recommend. Last year, (whoop, two years ago now what?) when the weather started fluctuating, I started to get worried about my instruments' humidification. Not unreasonably it seems as, once i got a decent digital hygrometer into my house, i was horrified with the results. I actually bought two: One analog and one digital. I spent about 30 bucks for the privilege. On a whim, i decided to buy these little guys for my instrument cases. I didn't think they would be very good, but I have been wrong. They nearly match my more expensive digital hygrometer and they are much more responsive than the more expensive analog one.. I put a few in some cases of pricier instruments and have peppered the rest in all the rooms of my house. They are consistently precise when i put them in the same room, for example, and I have found them to have very good accuracy. The batteries are button batteries and wear out fairly quickly but I have found them cheap to replace. If I had it to do again, I might have just bought these and skipped the 30 dollar trip to the hardware store. I really had no idea how dry it really gets in the winter shadow of my house until i looked. Glad I looked when i did. Honestly, I had no idea that humidification during that time would help me personally as much as it did. I expected my instruments to be okay, but that was also the first year i didn't get sick for a month since i've lived in this house. I couldn't have guessed how much the air quality would affect me. Nice tools to have carried into the year 2020 where air quality seemed to be one of those things that people were suddenly thinking about.

There are a plethora of these countertop icemakers being sold by Chinese companies on Amazon right now. They all were quite the same. I’ve used several of them, so I’m quite familiar with them. First of all… Though it shows this icemaker can make 26 pounds of ice in a twenty-four hour period. . . That is only if you continuously remove the ice from the basket. The basket holds enough ice to fill a 32 ounce water bottle.

Second… Once the ice has been made, this maker does not keep the ice frozen. The only way to keep the ice frozen is if you remove the ice from the basket and place it into your own freezer. The ice is quite “wet” so when you place it in your freezer it will freeze together and you will have to break it apart. If you do not remove the ice from the basket, then it simply melts and the water goes back down into the reservoir and it re-freezes. So is a continuous cycle of freezing and refreezing if you do not remove the ice. For this reason, you really should turn the machine off when you are not using it like when you are going away for a day or two… Or when you are sleeping.

Then I drain that and add fresh water and let that run a few times and then drain it again and add fresh water and do it one last time. I do this about once per month, and so for this is been working for me. I also have a bottle brush and I take that brush and dip it into the scaling powder solution and scrub the inside of the machine and then rinse.

I have done a lot of dishwasher troubleshooting as a manager of rental properties. Most dishwasher drain hoses I encounter are somewhat transparent. I can see water and debris flowing through them and can see accumulated debris. This is useful when troubleshooting a drainage issue or investigating a possible clog. While not essential, since transparent hoses are so readily available, why not get one of those instead of this opaque one? The transparent ones are the hazy white-colored one that allows light through. For the prior drainage issue I dealt with I was able to see the clog in the drainage hose, which I would not have been able to do if this opaque hose was installed.

This product does not come with clamps, which you should be using to secure the ends in place. If you are replacing a drain hose, then you already have the clamps.

Is this a dishwasher hose or a clothes-washing machine hose? It seems targeted at both since it has the bracket for a washing machine and the universal end for a dishwasher. Both hose types are essentially the same as long as they fit. This product is more suitable for a washing machine than a dishwasher, but it should work for both.

This is a fine dishwasher hose that you can cut to the right exit diameter. In addition to the exit diameter, make sure the end will fit as there are L-shaped and straight ends. For going into the garbage disposal, having a straight end at that location reduces clogging. Confirm the length you need. If you need to wrap the hose over the top of the dishwasher to get to the drain then 6 ft will not be long enough. This comes with two smaller clamps and one larger clamp, in addition to the extension connector and a hose holder if this is used with a clothes washing machine. For a washing machine, 6ft should be fine.

I have done a lot of dishwasher troubleshooting as a manager of rental properties. Most dishwasher drain hoses I encounter are somewhat transparent. I can see water and debris flowing through them and can see accumulated debris. This is useful when troubleshooting a drainage issue or investigating a possible clog. While not essential, since transparent hoses are so readily available, why not get one of those instead of this opaque one? The transparent ones are the hazy white-colored one that allows light through. I have never had a washing machine drain clog, so for that this opaque color is fine.

This is a generic Chinese hose and the identical product is being sold under different Amazon listings.
