There are a plethora of countertop icemakers being sold by mostly Chinese companies on Amazon right now. They are all very similar, with a few differences. The one main difference with this one is that it makes “nugget ice” and set up “tube ice”. The other thing that is “different” about this one is that it is super crazy over-the-top overpriced right now. More on that in a moment.

Make sure you understand exactly what this icemaker can and cannot do. This icemaker does not keep the ice frozen. Once the basket is filled, the machine will turn off and if you do not remove the ice, it will simply melt and the water goes back down into the reservoir, at which time the machine will turn back on and start making more ice. The only way to keep the ice frozen is to remove it from the basket and place it into your own freezer. But keep in mind the ice will be “wet” and you will need to break it apart when you remove it from the freezer.

The listing shows that this icemaker can make 30 pounds of ice per day. That is a bit of a misnomer. The only way that it can do that is if you continually remove the ice from the basket day and night. I highly doubt that someone is going to be up at 3 o’clock in the morning removing ice from this ice machine.

You really want to make sure that you turn the ice machine off when it is not in use like at night, and on weekends if you’re using it in an office. Because otherwise the machine will continually make ice… The ice will melt… And there were machine will make ice again. In a never- ending cycle.

This ice machine is made in China and probably being sold by Chinese company on Amazon, though they are using a US address. This icemaker is currently listed at 400 bucks. Currently there is an eighty dollar coupon that you will certainly want to click on if you purchase. But you can purchase “tube ice” countertop icemakers for well under 100 bucks. So unless you are just adamant about this particular machine, I highly recommend you look into the “tube ice countertop icemakers first.

There are quite a few of these icemakers being sold by assorted Chinese companies on Amazon right now. They are all virtually the same thing, though some of them look a little bit different. As long as your expectations meet what the icemaker can do, then it’s fine. But if your expectations exceed what the icemaker can do, then you will be disappointed.

Things to keep in mind…

First of all, this icemaker does not keep the ice frozen. The ice goes into a basket and then, if it is not used, it will melt and the water will fall to the bottom water reservoir and then it will be refrozen again and again through the machine. The only way to keep the ice frozen is if you remove it from the basket and place the ice into a freezer. But when you do that, the ice will be “wet” so it will freeze together and you will need to “bang” it apart.

Second… To say that this icemaker will make 26 pounds of ice each day is a bit of a misnomer. Because the only way for it to do that is if you continuously remove the ice from the basket each time the basket is full. It takes about an hour for the basket to fill up completely. So you would have to have someone removing the ice… Day and night… For it to make 26 pounds of ice. Of course you will have to continually fill the reservoir with water as well. So unless you are working in a factory or elsewhere that someone is there twenty-four hours a day, then you will not get 26 pounds of ice.

You should stop the icemaker from making ice when you are not using it. For example, in the evenings when you go to bed. Otherwise the ice will just continually melt and be recycled over and over and over.

This icemaker is made in China and being sold by Chinese company on Amazon. At the current price of 100 bucks it’s certainly twice the price it should be, but overall it is fine… Again… As long as you have the right expectations. This ice maker is compact. It is easy to set up and use. It is quick and not too noisy. The nugget style cubes are chewable. There are two sizes, small and large but the size difference is negligible. It has performed consistently.

The best repair guide can be found on YouTube under the title "Washing Machine Repair - Replacing the Drain Pump (LG Part # 4681EA2001T)." That's the video I followed and it took about an hour total. The hardest part is replacing the rubber drain collar around the door. Once you get that, it's game on.

I seriously think these stainless pour over coffee filters/drippers are one of the greatest inventions ever for coffee drinkers! There have been so many times where I have wanted a cup of ground coffee (not instant), but didn’t bother because I didn’t want to dirty the coffee maker just for one cup, and didn’t want to bother with the paper filters, etc. This pour-over filter lets you have that one cup of whatever coffee you have on hand, and you have total control over how weak or strong you want that coffee to be. However, it will hold enough ground coffee for more than one cup.

This filter is made of an ultra fine stainless steel mesh that you pour the coffee directly into, there is no need for a paper filter. The way this works is after you heat your water, place this filter over a coffee cup. This specific filter is especially nice because it has a wide base (3-5/8” or 9.2 cm diameter excluding the trim) and will fit over pretty much any drinking cup. Next, add your ground coffee into the filter. For my taste, I found that 1 heaping teaspoon of coffee is perfect. Then slowly pour your heated water directly into the filter over the coffee. There are 4 holes at the bottom of the base that enable you to see how full your coffee cup is. These holes also “catch” any coffee that has seeped through to the outside of the filter, this water will then flow through those holes right into your coffee cup. Really nice! My 20 year old dryer decided that it was going to heat at it's hottest setting to the point of scalding my hands when removing the clothes from the dryer and causing a major case of wrinkles in my work Polo's. After going to YouTube to find out how to diagnose the issue, I found that there are a few things to check. First thing you will need to do is open the back of the dryer, with it unplugged, and check the Thermal Fuse. This can be done with a multi-meter or temporarily jump the two connectors/blade terminals and check if the Dryer runs at the correct temp for all cycles. Since I had the dryer taken apart I figured I would clean out the blower fan area and the fan ducting as well as the entire "innards" of the dryer. After temporarily jumping the thermal fuse I found that it had kicked the bucket as the dryer started to work again due to jumping out the fuse. Did I say that this dryer is 20 years old and the original fuse lasted that long? So I decided that since I have the thing open I might as well replace the other 20 Year old electrical components that were back there. These Items included: the Thermal Fuse, Cycling Thermostat, High Limit Dryer Thermostat and Dryer Thermal cut off. Each have their own job and purpose, so don't skimp out and think you can get away with changing the item that has failed, because if that item failed the others will follow. Did I mention my Dryer is 20 years old? As A side note; I also checked the Heating Element and found that one of the coils had warped and contacted/welded itself the the element body, this is what took out the fuse. A pair of needle nose pliers and a steady hand detached the coil and re-positioned the coil in its original shape and placement. My 20 year old dryer, that was a wedding gift to my wife when she married her fist husband now works like a champ!

My LG LFXS30766S refrigerator was icing up in the refrigerator compartment behind the bottom drawer. One symptom was that the drain hole iced over, so when the defrost the water could not get into the bottom evaporator pan and I would have pooled water in the refrigerator, where it would eventually freeze.

I initially solved the clogging issue with a short copper wire. I had some scraps of electrical wire that I stripped off the coating and wrapped it around the defrost line and had the wire extend down into the drain hole. A YouTube video shows how this works. The concept is the defrost line heats up and the heat extends to the copper wire in the drain hole. This copper wire trick worked.

While searching for a solution I came across these drain clips and I figured they would work even better due to the larger surface area. The next time I had to work on my refrigerator I pushed the copper wire aside and attached this clip. I had to bend the tip so the tip was not touching the plastic drain tube. These are made for a Samsung, but they work fine in an LG, and are easier to install than a copper wire because the clip right to the defrost line instead of having to be wrapped around with pliers. I bought two of these in case I have to install the same thing in the freezer compartment, or in case I need to solve this same problem in another refrigerator.

An earlier clog with similar symptoms was caused by hard water deposits clogging the bottom of the drain tube, where it touches the evaporator pan in the back. I fixed this by cutting off the bottom of the drain tube to leave a gap between the drain tube and the pan.

My refrigerator was still icing over after the copper wire fix, although the problem of water not draining was addressed. I am swapping a replacement defrost sensor next to see if that helps, which is why I had the back off to install this drain clip.

This makes the cutest little ice cubs, I think they're perfect if you are someone who eats ice. For an ice chest you'll probably be working at it for a while as this thing makes a handful of cubes every few minutes. The thing I love about this ice maker is it has a smaller profile than many of them I've seen. Many are much larger and bulkier. This one's not too bad at all. After using this thing a few times I can say that we love it! Seems to be well made and works perfectly.

The small ice and large ice are the exact same size, the large ice just stays on the metal rods longer so they become thicker. Both of them come out thin enough I can put them in my hand and just crush them completely. I honestly love this ice and am very happy with this!

To make Ice you just fill the bottom reservoir with water up to it's "Max" fill line which is marked "Max" and then it sucks water from that up to the top reservoir where the metal rods are cooled to the point that ice starts forming on them. Once the ice is ready it will drop the ice and the little motorized scoop will scoop it down into the little ice tray. Very easy to use and fun to watch! It’s very important that you know exactly what you are getting with this machine. As long as you understand what you are getting and how the machine works, you will be fine. But if your expectations are too high, you may end up unhappy.

The pictures are a little deceiving. The top picture shows the icemaker chock full of ice. That is not how this machine works. You really need to watch the video to see how it works. There is a basket in the front where the ice is dropped and stored. When the small basket is full, the machine will stop producing ice. I have a 32 ounce water bottle and the basket will feel my water bottle with ice about two thirds full. The basket area is not cold like a freezer. So the ice will continue to melt… With the water flowing down into the water reservoir area… And more ice will be made. The only way you can continually make and save nice is if you remove the basket, about once per hour, and place the ice into a receptacle and place it in your freezer.

The listing shows that this icemaker will make 26 pounds of ice and 24 hours. Well, that’s only if you continually add water and continually remove the basket of ice and place the ice in your freezer. So unless you can do that every hour… Day and night… You are not going to end up with 26 pounds of ice.

I like this icemaker for what it is. And as long as you understand how it works, and don’t have extraordinarily high expectations, then you too may like this icemaker.

There are a lot of these countertop icemakers being sold by Chinese companies on Amazon right now. Most of them work exactly the same, though they may look slightly different. The bin holds enough ice to fill a 32 ounce water bottle. It takes approximately one hour for the bin to fill. So someone would have to remove the ice day and night to actually make 26 pounds worth of ice. If you do not remove the eyes, then it simply melts and is recycled again and again. The ice is not kept frozen inside the machine. The only way to keep the ice frozen would be to remove it and place it in your own freezer. On top of this, the ice is “wet” and will freeze together if you place it in your own freezer. So you will need to break it apart to use it. Also, this ice machine is not connected to a water source. You must pour water into the machine for it to make ice.

By ice maker in my freezer stopped working a while ago. But the overall refrigerator freezer works just fine. So having this separate icemaker works for me. I know some others who use them in a small office environment… And a motorhome… And so on.

This ice machine is made in China and being sold by Chinese company on Amazon. Again, there are several Chinese companies selling similar ice machines on Amazon right now. So look around before purchasing for the best price. Some also offer a timer, which is nice so that the ice machine is not operating when you are sleeping. Otherwise, if you leave it on at night, then the ice will simply refreeze again and again.

My 20 year old dryer decided that it was going to heat at it's hottest setting to the point of scalding my hands when removing the clothes from the dryer and causing a major case of wrinkles in my work Polo's. After going to YouTube to find out how to diagnose the issue, I found that there are a few things to check. First thing you will need to do is open the back of the dryer, with it unplugged, and check the Thermal Fuse. This can be done with a multi-meter or temporarily jump the two connectors/blade terminals and check if the Dryer runs at the correct temp for all cycles. Since I had the dryer taken apart I figured I would clean out the blower fan area and the fan ducting as well as the entire "innards" of the dryer. After temporarily jumping the thermal fuse I found that it had kicked the bucket as the dryer started to work again due to jumping out the fuse. Did I say that this dryer is 20 years old and the original fuse lasted that long? So I decided that since I have the thing open I might as well replace the other 20 Year old electrical components that were back there. These Items included: the Thermal Fuse, Cycling Thermostat, High Limit Dryer Thermostat and Dryer Thermal cut off. Each have their own job and purpose, so don't skimp out and think you can get away with changing the item that has failed, because if that item failed the others will follow. Did I mention my Dryer is 20 years old? As A side note; I also checked the Heating Element and found that one of the coils had warped and contacted/welded itself the the element body, this is what took out the fuse. A pair of needle nose pliers and a steady hand detached the coil and re-positioned the coil in its original shape and placement. My 20 year old dryer, that was a wedding gift to my wife when she married her fist husband now works like a champ!

Our icemaker in our freezer just doesn't want to work, and making ice the old fashioned way gets old. This allows us to either make ice on demand or make a bunch and keep in the freezer (we tend to do both--make ice when needed and make extra for in between). The ice it makes is the hollow tube type, which is good for making quick ice and quickly melts in your beverage.

Setup took seconds, and it's easy to drain and keep ready for the next go round. It's not too bulky, so you can keep it out on a counter or bar, but that does mean that the compact basket needs to be periodically emptied. It lacks any form of plumbing, but the water receptacle is plenty big. If anything I wish that the ice basket were larger to allow it to essentially fill around the same time as the water runs out. The other quirk is that the ice comes out wet and just barely frozen. If you put into a freezer, it will stick to other ice and make a block of ice. As long as I break it up in an hour or so, it stays separated. These quirks aside, I have no complaints.

Highly recommended Saying that this ice machine can produce 26# of ice is a little “unrealistic”. Can it produce that much in that amount of time? Probably. . . But. . . It means that someone has to be willing to empty the small ice bin when it fills. . . and keep the water reservoir filled . . .continually. . .for 24-hours. Again. . . Unrealistic.

The small ice bin holds no more than a pound of ice. . . if that. When full, the basket fills my 32oz water bottle about 2/3 full. The inside is not at freezing temperature. So . . .Unless you remove the ice, and place it in your regular freezer, the ice will simply melt. . . and then get reprocessed. The machine will stop making ice when it fills. If you remove the ice from the container, and place it in your freezer, it will then freeze together. So you will have to break it apart.

Don’t get me wrong. . . For what it is. . . I like it. But you just have to make sure your expectations meet what this ice machine will actually do.
